where: an ix VM used for timing
what: The same binary's cold hello-world build took 17 to 48 s and the same first build of a new project 13 to 34 s across an hour on one VM (`khugepaged` at 9% of a core, the guest's memory growing from 3 to 47 GiB as it was used, `the flight recorder lost rows`): medians of five moved by a factor of two between two runs of the same script.
cost: two measuring runs thrown away; every claim made from an interleaved run and a matched pair instead of medians
cause: unknown: the VM was made without `--memory-commit` or a CPU class, as the brief's command said
workaround: interleave the binaries round by round (abab.py) and read CPU time and counts beside wall time
state: open: a lane that measures should get `--memory-commit` and `--cpu` in its brief's `ix new`
